content: 1. Eliglustat: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors are contraindicated in patients who are poor or intermediate metabolizers of eliglustat. For extensive metabolizers, reduce the eliglustat dose from 84 mg twice daily to 84 mg once daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Eliglustat is contraindicated if strong or moderate CYP2D6 inhibitors are used concurrently with strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors. 2. Isoniazid and Eluxadoline: Isoniazid increases eluxadoline levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Due to incomplete information on eluxadoline metabolism, exercise caution when co-administering with strong CYP2C19 inhibitors. 3. Isoniazid and Elvitegravir: Isoniazid increases elvitegravir levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Elvitegravir, a CYP3A4 substrate, may have increased levels when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 4. Isoniazid and Encorafenib: Isoniazid increases encorafenib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is unavoidable, reduce the encorafenib dose to one-third of the original dose (e.g., from 450 mg/day to 150 mg/day). Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 5. Isoniazid and Enfortumab Vedotin: Isoniazid increases enfortumab vedotin toxicity by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Enfortumab vedotin releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), which is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4. Co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase MMAE exposure, leading to higher toxicity risks. 6. Isoniazid and Entrectinib: Isoniazid increases entrectinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid co-administration of moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors with entrectinib. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the moderate CYP3A inhibitor for 3-5 elimination half-lives. 7. Isoniazid and Eplerenone: Isoniazid increases eplerenone levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Isoniazid and Erdafitinib: Isoniazid increases erdafitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. 9. Isoniazid and Ergotamine: Isoniazid increases ergotamine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Both drugs increase serotonin levels, which may lead to serotonin syndrome. 10. Isoniazid and Escitalopram: Isoniazid increases escitalopram levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Both drugs increase serotonin levels, which may increase the risk of serotonin syndrome. 11. Isoniazid and Esomeprazole: Isoniazid increases esomeprazole levels by affecting CYP2C19 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 12. Isoniazid and Ethanol: Isoniazid increases ethanol toxicity by decreasing its metabolism, leading to enhanced hepatotoxicity. Avoid co-administration when possible. 13. Isoniazid and Ethionamide: Ethionamide increases isoniazid levels through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Isoniazid and Fentanyl: Isoniazid increases fentanyl levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is necessary, monitor patients for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust fentanyl doses as needed. 15. Isoniazid and Flibanserin: Isoniazid increases flibanserin levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors is contraindicated. 16. Isoniazid and Gefitinib: Isoniazid increases gefitinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 17. Isoniazid and Gilteritinib: Isoniazid increases gilteritinib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor closely for gilteritinib-related adverse effects and adjust the dosage as needed. 18. Isoniazid and Glasdegib: Isoniazid increases glasdegib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
